summary: Canada's police report the racialized and Indigenous identity of homicide victims and accused, but no other police-reported crime carries race or Indigenous identity yet (national collection is not expected before 2027). Statistics Canada's racialized categories never separate White people: 'rest of the population' combines White and Indigenous people.

nations.Federal (Statistics Canada): Homicide Survey with racialized and Indigenous identity since 2019 (Indigenous since 2014); UCR crime counts without identity; safety surveys by visible-minority status and Indigenous identity.
nations.Provinces: Child welfare is provincial; no national official child-welfare statistics by race. The CIS study (non-government) fills part of the gap every five to ten years.

european_title: Not separately identified by any Canadian official source
european_note: Statistics Canada measures 'racialized' people with the visible-minority standard. Everyone else (White and Indigenous people) is grouped as 'rest of the population' or 'not a visible minority', so White or ethnic European people are never separately identified in official crime or survey tables. Only the non-government CIS child-welfare study reports White children separately.

harms.label: Homicide
harms.intro: Police reported 37 homicide victims under 18 in 2025 (15 aged 0-11), and 672 victims of all ages. Child victims are published by Indigenous identity only; racialized identity is published for all ages, for victims and for people accused.

victims.n_label: child victims with known Indigenous identity (of 37)
victims.rate_reason: No child population by Indigenous identity is published with this table; rates are not calculated here.
victims.share_note: Indigenous identity only (First Nations, Métis, Inuit). 'Non-Indigenous' combines White and racialized children. Small numbers: over 2023-2025, 57 of 169 child victims with known identity were Indigenous (33.7%). No matching child population by Indigenous identity is used here, so no over-representation ratio is calculated.

perpetrators.scope: Canada, persons accused of homicide, all ages and all victims, 2025
perpetrators.rate_label: persons accused of homicide per 100,000 people of the same group (all ages)
perpetrators.rate_note: Official Statistics Canada rates (table 35-10-0207-01). Crude rates, not adjusted for age or sex.
perpetrators.share_note: Police-reported racialized identity (Statistics Canada's 'visible minority' standard). 'Rest of the population' (shown here as Not racialized) combines White people with Indigenous people, who are not counted as a visible minority, so White or ethnic European people are not separately identified. Identity is determined by police from information found with the person, family, community members or other sources. Covers all victims, not only children. Rough derivation, calculated here across two tables: of the 416 'rest of the population' accused, 185 were Indigenous (table 35-10-0060-01), leaving roughly 231 (about 39%) neither racialized nor Indigenous, i.e. mostly White.

cross.text: Statistics Canada links victims' racialized identity only to their relationship with the accused (table 35-10-0208-01), not to the accused person's identity. No victim-by-accused identity table, and none for child victims.

harms.label: Child-welfare investigations (abuse and neglect)
harms.intro: An estimated 299,217 child-maltreatment-related investigations were conducted in Canada in 2019 (Canadian Incidence Study, CIS-2019). Neglect, physical abuse, sexual abuse, emotional maltreatment and exposure to intimate partner violence are all included.

victims.scope: Canada, maltreatment-related investigations of children aged 15 and under, 2019
victims.rate_label: investigations per 1,000 children of the same group aged 15 and under
victims.rate_note: Published by the study team (Figure 1 of the CIS-2019 Latin American report). Investigations, not substantiated cases.
victims.share_note: Non-government source. 153,372 investigations involved White children and 5,902 Latin American children; this report does not give the other groups. A 2025 analysis of the same study (excluding Quebec) found 115.6 investigations per 1,000 Black children vs 51.0 per 1,000 White children.

perpetrators.text: The study records caregivers' characteristics, but no national table of the ethno-racial identity of the alleged perpetrator was found.

harms.label: Online child sexual exploitation
harms.intro: Police reported 15,075 incidents of child sexual abuse and exploitation material (5,867 possessing or accessing; 9,208 making or distributing) and 3,556 incidents of luring a child via a computer in 2025 (table 35-10-0177-01).

victims.text: Children shown in material are usually unidentified, and police data carry no race or Indigenous identity yet.

perpetrators.text: Not recorded in police-reported crime data yet (national collection not before 2027).

breakdown.why: Police record 13,576 sexual violations against children (2025) but no race or Indigenous identity until national PIRID data (not before 2027). Only the 2018 SSPPS survey gives childhood sexual abuse by visible-minority status and Indigenous identity; 'not a visible minority' lumps White with Indigenous people, so ethnic Europeans are not separate.

SSPPS 2018 childhood physical abuse by visible-minority status and Indigenous identity (lumped), plus the non-government CIS-2019 child-welfare study, which does separate White children. No perpetrator heritage anywhere.
Only the non-government CIS-2019 (White children separately identified, 2019 data); no official national child-welfare statistics by race.

Homicide Survey: victims and accused by police-reported racialized identity (all ages, 1.8% and 0.5% unknown) and Indigenous identity (child victims 0-17). 'Rest of the population' lumps White with Indigenous people, so ethnic Europeans are not separate; official rates; no victim-by-accused identity table.

components.name: Victim heritage
components.full: Official data by harm that separately identify ethnic European children (e.g. White non-Hispanic, White British) alongside every other group, self-reported or official, few unknowns. Broad categories that lump ethnic Europeans with others get partial credit; proxies (nationality, citizenship, migration background, country of birth) at most 9.4 points.

components.name: Perpetrator heritage
components.full: Same standard for perpetrators: not perceived, few unknowns, ethnic Europeans separately identified. Proxies at most 9.4 points.

components.name: Coverage and missing data
components.full: Over 90% of the population covered, under 10% unknown

components.name: Rates and linkage
components.full: Rates per 100,000 possible, and victim heritage linked to perpetrator heritage

score.gold_standard: 100% means a country publishes data that separately identifies ethnic Europeans, both as perpetrators (so one can tell when they disproportionately harm a group) and as child victims (so one can tell when ethnic European children are disproportionately harmed), alongside every other group, linked victim to perpetrator, for every harm.
score.rules: Heritage is 75 of every 100 points (victims 37.5, perpetrators 37.5); coverage, rates and access share the other 25. Proxies such as nationality or migration background earn at most a quarter of the heritage points. A country with no real ethnicity data for victims or perpetrators is capped at 25%.
score.why: Canada scores 25% on the stricter scale (20-40%). Homicide is well covered: police report the racialized and Indigenous identity of victims and accused, with official rates. For every other harm, the police record no race or Indigenous identity yet (national collection is not expected before 2027), so heritage data come only from a 2018 adult survey and a non-government child-welfare study. Even the homicide data lump White people with Indigenous people as 'rest of the population', so ethnic Europeans are never separately identified in official data.
score.weights_id: harm weights of 19 Nov 2026 (homicide 25, sexual abuse 20, sex trafficking 20, physical abuse 15, online exploitation 10, neglect 10)

hs_indig.name: Homicide Survey: victims and accused by Indigenous identity, age group and gender (table 35-10-0060-01)
hs_indig.records: Homicide victims and accused by police-reported Indigenous identity and age group, including 0-11 and 12-17.
hs_indig.limitations: Indigenous vs non-Indigenous only; 'non-Indigenous' combines White and racialized people. Accused are classed by their own age, not the victim's.

hs_victims.name: Homicide Survey: victims by racialized identity group (table 35-10-0206-01)
hs_victims.records: Number, share and rate of homicide victims by racialized (visible-minority) group, gender and region.
hs_victims.limitations: No age breakdown. 'Rest of the population' lumps White and Indigenous victims. Police-determined identity.

hs_accused.name: Homicide Survey: persons accused by racialized identity group (table 35-10-0207-01)
hs_accused.records: Number, share and rate of persons accused of homicide by racialized group, gender and region.
hs_accused.limitations: No victim age. 'Rest of the population' lumps White and Indigenous accused.

hs_rel.name: Homicide Survey: victims of solved homicides by racialized identity and accused-victim relationship (table 35-10-0208-01)
hs_rel.records: Victims by racialized group and relationship to the accused (family, acquaintance, stranger...).
hs_rel.limitations: Links victim identity to relationship, not to the accused's identity.

ucr.name: Incident-based crime statistics by detailed violation (table 35-10-0177-01)
ucr.records: Police-reported incidents and rates by violation, including sexual violations against children, child sexual abuse and exploitation material, luring and trafficking in persons.
ucr.limitations: Counts of incidents; no race or Indigenous identity of victims or accused.

pirid.name: Police-reported Indigenous and Racialized Identity Data (PIRID) through the UCR Survey: progress update
pirid.publisher: Statistics Canada and Canadian Association of Chiefs of Police
pirid.years: Collection possible since Feb 2024 (UCR 2.5); update June 2025
pirid.records: Plan to record the Indigenous and racialized identity of all victims and accused in police-reported crime, by officer perception or self-identification.
pirid.limitations: Adoption by police services is voluntary; 'national-level data are not expected to be received until at least 2027'.

sspps.name: Survey of Safety in Public and Private Spaces 2018: self-reported physical and sexual abuse during childhood (table 35-10-0167-01)
sspps.records: Share of people aged 15+ who were physically or sexually abused by an adult before age 15, by visible-minority status, Indigenous identity, immigrant status and other characteristics.
sspps.limitations: Retrospective adult recall; 2018 data. 'Not a visible minority' combines White and Indigenous people. No perpetrator identity.

chscy.name: Canadian Health Survey on Children and Youth 2023: child maltreatment (PHAC analysis, Feb 2026)
chscy.publisher: Public Health Agency of Canada / Statistics Canada
chscy.records: Youth aged 15-17 self-reporting maltreatment (physical abuse 22.3%, sexual abuse 5.3%).
chscy.limitations: Published by gender only; racialized and Indigenous identity exist only in the microdata; excludes reserves and foster care.

cis2019.name: Canadian Incidence Study of Reported Child Abuse and Neglect 2019 (CIS-2019): Latin American children report
cis2019.publisher: CIS research team (Toronto Metropolitan University, McGill, University of Toronto); study funded by the Public Health Agency of Canada
cis2019.records: Estimated child-welfare investigations and rates per 1,000 children by ethno-racial category of the child.
cis2019.limitations: Non-government academic source. Investigations, not confirmed abuse. Only every five to ten years; this report gives White and Latin American children only.

bk2025.name: Boatswain-Kyte et al. (2025), Racial disparities in child welfare: Black and White children in Canada, Child Abuse & Neglect 169
bk2025.records: Investigation and placement rates for Black and White children.

availability_note: Each harm has an 'availability' map listing the victim and perpetrator groups with any published figure (overall and by measure) and any linked victim-perpetrator pairs. Groups not listed have no data for that harm; the explorer should grey them out rather than offer an empty combination.
